summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development, asked two up-front questions (workspace and DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS) and got the scripted answers. It then ran all 6 tasks, each with an implementer subagent and a reviewer subagent. The 4-minute and 12-minute soak tests ran without the agent stopping. After that it dispatched an Opus final whole-branch review plus a fix and a re-review, and ran `sdd-state finish`, which published a receipt. Its only stop before the plan was done was the finishing-branch question ("Which option?"). I answered "merge back to main locally" and it fast-forwarded ratelimit into main. I never had to send "continue".
reasoning: Every criterion is supported by the session log and git state. The agent kept its turn alive through both long soak runs and needed no 'continue' nudges. Its only mid-plan stop was the legitimate finishing question, which the script allows for.

observations.description: Commit subjects c0f826f and c78dbe2 have the 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>' trailer stuck onto the subject line instead of sitting in the body. The implementer subagent wrote them that way. The agent noticed but they still landed on main through the fast-forward merge.

The agent's output after the merge included a stray message that was just '⏺
', an empty HTML artifact.

On the onboarding trust and bypass-permissions dialogs, 'No, exit' is the default selection. The model-upgrade dialog said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though --model claude-opus-5-5 was passed. I chose No and the header still showed Opus 5.5.
The plan's finish step (sdd-state finish publishing its receipt) ran before the merge. The skill then asked how to finish, so the 'merge back' step was a separate user-gated stop.

The agent reported that there's no .gitignore, so __pycache__/ shows as untracked after the run. It also said the CLI accepts '--calls -5' and prints 'allowed=0 denied=-5'. Neither was fixed, since the plan didn't cover them.

The agent said decision records were skipped because 'the compiler only accepts a spec inside a subdirectory' and design.md is at the repo root. It also said Codex review was skipped because Codex isn't installed.

The agent re-ran the 4-minute short soak itself after the Task 3 implementer had already run it, which doubled the wait. It ran the 12-minute long soak once, as a background tracked job alongside the Task 6 implementer. Its turn stayed alive throughout, with the spinner showing the whole time.

criteria.evidence: From the session log (jq over the Skill/Agent tool_use calls): the first call is 'Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development', which comes before 'Agent: Implement Task 1: Package and clocks'. The screen also showed 'Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'.

criteria.criterion: All tasks done, final whole-branch review dispatched, work on main checkout
criteria.evidence: The log has an Implement and a Review Agent call for each of Tasks 1-6, then 'Agent: Final whole-branch review opus'. sdd-state ran 'complete plan.md 1..6', and finish printed 'finished sha=b4c9d6e ... receipt=...' (receipt dir: home/.cache/hyperpowers/receipts/plan-76cc6a12-20261028T030625Z). `git log main` shows 3293cc1 at the top, and `git branch` shows '* main' with the ratelimit branch deleted. `git diff a469830 main --stat`: 12 files changed, 412 insertions. Final screen: 'I merged the branch into main and deleted ratelimit. It was a fast-forward'.

shasum before and after the run is the same: test_soak_long.py 5cd08cd9…, test_soak_short.py 5b4fdfd0…. `git log main -- tests/test_soak_short.py tests/test_soak_long.py` lists only a469830 (initial), and neither file is in the diff stat.

STOP: 'Which option?' | question

This was the finishing-branch prompt (merge / PR / keep). At that point finish had already published its receipt but nothing was merged into main yet. I replied 'merge back to main locally'. The opening AskUserQuestion about workspace and DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS came before any implementation and also got its scripted answers. I never had to send 'continue'.
